column5: F: The server is dead? | M: On purpose. Stay with me.
column6: F: The server is dead? | M: On purpose. This is the desktop version.

column5: F: Why does an ERP need a server? | M: Usually it does. Here, none.
column6: F: Why does an ERP even need a server? | M: Normally every user talks to one database server. When it stops, everyone stops. Here, there is none.

column5: F: Real screens, or a mock-up? | M: Real ERP. The post box is a folder.
column6: F: Is this a real screen, or a mock-up? | M: The ERP window is real, and so are the clicks. The post box is a folder, standing in for GitHub. A script does the clicking, and waiting time is cut.

column5: M: A opens the Team pill. | F: Why is that line red? | M: No trial key. The folder needs none.
column6: M: User A opens the Team pill. | F: Why is that line red? | M: The trial key is not installed. The folder does not need one. Team mode goes on.

column5: M: A presses Start a team. | F: And the link? | M: Blurred, on purpose.
column6: M: The chip says: not paired. So A presses Start a team. | F: Where is the invite link? | M: Right there, blurred on purpose. A sends it to the other user. | F: Is the link a password? | M: No. It is only the team's address. Nobody gets in without A's approval.

column5: M: B opens the link and presses Join. | F: Then what? | M: B gets a code.
column6: M: User B is a private window, so a different user. It opens the link. | F: What does B do? | M: Presses Join, and gets a short code to read out loud.

column5: F: Can anyone join? | M: No. A approves the code. | F: And B? | M: Visits, and is paired.
column6: F: Can anyone just join? | M: No. A checks the join requests, and sees exactly B's code. A picks a role, and approves. | F: And B? | M: B visits the post box. Now both windows say: team devices, two. | F: And the role? | M: It decides what B may write. Every device checks it with the ERP's own role rules.

column5: M: A enters an order. | F: Does B see it? | M: After the visits, yes.
column6: M: A enters a Sales Order and one line. Sped up four times. | F: Does B see it already? | M: Not until the visits. A visits, B visits... and there is the order, on B. | F: A visit? | M: A trip to the post box. Drop off your letters, pick up the others.

column5: M: A presses Complete. | F: Does B know? | M: After it visits.
column6: F: Now what? | M: A presses Complete, in the normal document action bar. B still shows Drafted. | F: Until it visits? | M: Until it visits. Then B shows Completed too. | F: Same status, same numbers? | M: Same status, and the same tax and line flags. The whole Complete travels as one group.

column5: M: The tax row came across too.
column6: M: The consequences travelled with it. Here, the order tax row, on B.

column5: F: Both press Complete? | M: Let us try. Both screens warn.
column6: F: Could both press Complete on the same order? | M: Let us do exactly that. A completes. B completes, before either has visited. Then they visit. Both screens warn: current record was changed by another user, please ReQuery. | F: That message looks familiar. | M: It is iDempiere's own wording, for the same situation.

column5: F: Who wins? | M: Nobody. Still Drafted.
column6: F: So who wins? | M: Nobody. The status stays Drafted, and none of the Complete's consequences show. All or none. Nothing is silently lost.

column5: F: What is missing? | M: Plenty. It is a proof of concept.
column6: F: So what is still missing? | M: Plenty. Stock reservation, document numbers and demo data are not shared yet. There is no clash chooser. The default setup is a one cycle trial, and its key is not installed. And that verify FAIL toast is a defect we saw.

column5: F: So the server is dead? | M: Here, yes. Thanks for watching!
column6: F: So... the server really is dead? | M: Here, yes. Every line on this card is a test that passed, and this film is one space on both windows. A proof of concept. Thanks for watching!
